GatewayFeatureState.description:
Whether a Gateway serves one of its features: the cache or
handles. Each needs a Gateway database (databaseId), and the data plane
serves it only while the deployment's own switch for it (cache.enabled
or compression.enabled) is on as well. Turning a feature off deletes
nothing: stored entries expire on their TTL, so turning it back on with the
same Gateway database finds the ones still live.

info.description:
Administration API for Context Gateway resources and their Upstreams.

Every write completes synchronously and returns the final state. Creating an
Upstream, changing its mcp endpoint or authentication, and refreshing its catalog
run live discovery against the Upstream, bounded by the discovery timeout.

An Upstream carries the members every kind shares at the top level and its
kind's own settings in one object named after the kind: mcp or contextSurface.
A new kind adds an optional object member and an UpstreamKind value, so a
client that does not know the kind still reads every shared member and ignores
the object.
The tenant comes from the control-plane configuration, never from the request,
and no response shows it.
